text: Wazuh’s example rule 100603 contains a field pattern !mms-automation alongside its failed-authentication match. The field reference documents negate as an explicit attribute, defaulting to no, and repeated field conditions as logical AND. The article does not demonstrate that its leading-exclamation pattern excludes automation records. Do not treat that snippet as a verified exclusion or attribution mechanism; preserve the original automation principal when investigating the Atlas identity substitution that MongoDB documents. (medium confidence)
keywords: Correlating Atlas control-plane and database audit actors

text: To isolate additional Data Explorer activity, MongoDB documents database-audit role filters for atlasDataAccessReadWrite, atlasDataAccessReadOnly and atlasDataAccessAdmin on admin. These role filters identify relevant activity; the documentation does not say the shared role name uniquely identifies a human. (low confidence)

text: The Activity Feed documentation for the updated Data Explorer says individual CRUD operations and regular index builds no longer generate feed entries. It records user connections on opening Data Explorer and one listIndexStats entry on accessing a collection, with the Atlas username, regardless of subsequent reads or writes. Those entries cannot alone establish a one-to-one user-to-CRUD mapping. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: Correlating Atlas control-plane and database audit actors

text: The operator audit documentation says Atlas audit logs do not track user creation or modification events because Atlas performs these operations directly in admin. An investigator cannot use the absence of those database-audit records to rule out a control-plane user-management change. (low confidence)
keywords: Correlating Atlas control-plane and database audit actors

text: Elastic Atlas integration 1.3.1 demonstrates a useful actor-versus-target distinction: its organization event sample stores the actor in user.name/user.id and a different account in mongodb_atlas.organization.target.username; related.user contains both. Correlation code should preserve this distinction rather than treating every related username as the initiator. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
keywords: Correlating Atlas control-plane and database audit actors

text: For an Atlas user action in the Atlas UI on a cluster, the operator audit documentation says both audit logs and mongodb.log record mms-automation as the database user, while the Project Activity Feed records the actual Atlas username. Preserve the executing database principal and initiating Atlas identity as separate evidence fields. (low confidence)
keywords: Correlating Atlas control-plane and database audit actors

text: The MongoDB mongo-schema reference defines audit uuid as a client-connection identifier for grouping that client’s audit events. Elastic Atlas integration 1.3.1 exposes audit UUID separately from organization event.id. Do not equate those fields or infer a global event ID joining database operations to Activity Feed. (high confidence)
keywords: Correlating Atlas control-plane and database audit actors

text: Recommended investigation method, inferred from the documented fields: narrow the Project Activity Feed by project, cluster, event type, time range and Initiated By, then compare candidate database records by event time, action/command and parameters, namespace, result and host. Preserve the original Atlas actor and database users as separate fields, and label unresolved or multiple candidate matches as ambiguous; these documents do not establish an exact cross-plane join. (medium confidence)
keywords: Correlating Atlas control-plane and database audit actors

text: In Elastic MongoDB Atlas Integration 1.3.1, the project-event example separates top-level user.id/user.name from mongodb_atlas.project.database.username and mongodb_atlas.project.target.username. The latter fields describe the database user changed and the console user targeted. Do not treat a target username as the initiating actor. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
keywords: Correlating Atlas control-plane and database audit actors
